correctness.rationale: Each ball lifts to at most the sum of its future residual layer sizes. Adjacent layer sums are bounded by U+1; even/odd pairings give the exact finite ceiling. For fixed q, short balls contain at most a constant number of states while long balls have average layer density at most U/2+o(U). The binary copy-with-gap languages have U=2^(d+1)-1 and at least 2^d(T+1) distinct residuals in a root ball of radius d+T, proving the constant 1/2 sharp when T=d^2. The independent literal-word checker reconstructed 24 witness languages and 1000 seeded random languages; finite checks corroborate but do not prove the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: The sharp factor-two asymptotic separation is a structural obstruction to equality of the two natural, efficiently computable bounds at unbounded bandwidth over any fixed alphabet. It answers the high-value unbounded regime of a concrete fixed-alphabet question in the originating paper and gives explicit binary witnesses showing the constant cannot be strengthened. The result is not a parameter-renamed existing inequality, finite table lookup or numerical exercise.
